key_insight: Coding agents can directly search for explicit, interpretable feedback laws for active flow control and achieve DRL-level or better performance.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical alternative to black-box reinforcement learning for flow-control systems where simulator cost, partial observability, and interpretability matter.
method: Use a constrained heuristic-learning protocol with a coding agent proposing executable controllers.
Evaluate and revise controller code only through the public benchmark interface.
Compare learned heuristics against strong DRL baselines under identical simulation budgets across 13 benchmarks.
evidence_signal: Across 13 active flow-control benchmarks in 1D, 2D, and 3D, the discovered controllers matched or outperformed the best DRL policy in 10 environments under the same simulation budget.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of the benchmark interface and careful constraint design, so results may not transfer unchanged to closed or more complex real-world control setups.
paper_title: Heuristic Learning for Active Flow Control Using Coding Agents
